condition: Diabetes (Type 2): Awareness, Symptoms, and When to Seek Care

source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for Diabetes Mellitus Type 2
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

scope_note: AIRA covers diabetes awareness, symptom recognition, and triage only. Diabetes management, medication, and dose advice must come from a doctor.

sections.label: Diabetic Emergency Signs: Go to Hospital Immediately
items: Hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar), symptoms: trembling or shaking, sudden sweating, anxiety or irritability, confusion, fast heartbeat, dizziness, blurred vision, weakness, seizures, or unconsciousness. These can occur if a person with diabetes skips meals or takes too much diabetes medicine. Immediate action: if the person is conscious and able to swallow, give sugar immediately, loose sugar, a sweet biscuit, misri (rock candy), or any sweet drink. If unconscious, do not give anything by mouth, go to hospital immediately.
Very high blood sugar with confusion, rapid breathing, and extreme thirst, may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), which is a medical emergency
Chest pain or severe breathlessness in a person with diabetes, diabetes significantly increases the risk of heart attack
Stroke warning signs in a person with diabetes: sudden one-sided weakness, speech difficulty, severe headache, vision loss, go to hospital immediately
Non-healing wound or foot ulcer with spreading redness, swelling, pus, or bad smell, diabetic foot infections can become life-threatening quickly
High fever with severe infection signs in a diabetic person, diabetes worsens the severity of infections

sections.label: Daily Self-Care for Persons with Diabetes
items: Take your diabetes medicines exactly as prescribed by your doctor, do not stop or change the dose on your own
Eat regular meals at consistent times, skipping meals can cause low blood sugar in those on certain diabetes medicines
Always carry something sweet (sugar, misri, a biscuit) in case of low blood sugar symptoms
Follow a diet low in refined sugar, white rice, maida, and sweet drinks. Eat more vegetables, whole grains, pulses, and fruits in moderate amounts
Be physically active, at least 30 minutes of walking or light exercise daily helps control blood sugar
Do not smoke, smoking dramatically increases the risk of heart attack and kidney damage in diabetics
Avoid alcohol or use it very minimally
Inspect your feet every day for cuts, blisters, redness, swelling, or wounds, even small injuries can become serious in diabetics
Wear proper footwear at all times, avoid going barefoot
Monitor your blood sugar regularly as advised by your doctor
Keep all follow-up appointments, diabetes requires regular monitoring of blood sugar, blood pressure, kidney function, and eyes

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Symptoms that may suggest undiagnosed diabetes: frequent urination, excessive thirst, increased hunger, unexplained weight loss, extreme tiredness, blurred vision, slow-healing wounds, or recurring infections
Blood sugar reading on a home glucometer that is consistently high
Any person above 30 years of age who is overweight, has a family history of diabetes, or has high blood pressure, they should be screened annually
Any wound or cut on the foot in a diabetic that is not healing within a few days
Recurring infections: skin infections, fungal infections, urinary infections, or oral thrush in a person not known to be diabetic
A diabetic person whose blood sugar is not well controlled despite following advice
A diabetic person starting any new illness, even a common cold or fever needs closer monitoring

sections.label: Go to Hospital Without Delay
items: Any emergency danger sign listed above, hypoglycaemia with unconsciousness, chest pain, stroke signs, severe infection, spreading foot wound
A diabetic person who is very unwell, confused, or unable to eat or drink
Diabetic foot ulcer with spreading redness or foul smell, this requires urgent specialist care to prevent amputation
A diabetic with very high or very low blood sugar readings and symptoms

screening_note.label: Who Should Be Screened for Diabetes
items: All adults above 30 years of age, at least once a year
Anyone who is overweight or obese
Anyone with a first-degree relative (parent or sibling) with diabetes
Anyone with high blood pressure or high cholesterol
Women with a history of diabetes during pregnancy (gestational diabetes)
Anyone with symptoms: frequent urination, excessive thirst, unexplained weight loss, repeated infections, or slow-healing wounds

review.notes: All drug names, HbA1c thresholds for treatment decisions, and prescribing algorithms excluded. Hypoglycaemia emergency retained in full including the immediate sugar treatment, this is a first-aid response, not a prescribing recommendation, and is directly sourced from the NCD ASHA module page 38. Foot care and infection warning signs retained as critical for Indian diabetic patients.
